title: How to Fix Blurry Product Photos (Before Reshooting the Whole Catalog)
description: Blurry product photos don't always need reshoots. Here's what AI can salvage and when to accept defeat.

blocks.text: You went through all your product photos and realized half are slightly blurry. Reshooting 50 products sounds miserable. Is there another way?
Yes. Sometimes.
The Two Types of Blur
Motion blur: Camera moved during exposure. Usually unrecoverable.
Slight softness: Focus was slightly off, or resolution is low. Often recoverable.
Diagnose which type you have. Motion blur = reshoot. Softness = try editing.
What AI Can Fix
Modern AI upscaling and sharpening tools can:
Background removal cannot restore detail lost to blur. Test a mild upscale in a separate editor only when the source still contains usable detail, and review the result at 100% before publishing.
What AI Can't Fix

items.text: Blur that spans the entire product

blocks.text: If your photo is fundamentally broken, no amount of AI enhances it. Reshoot.
The Sharpening Trick
For slightly soft photos:

items.text: Use a separate upscaling or sharpening editor conservatively, then inspect the result at 100% for invented texture and halos.

blocks.text: Result: Photos that were borderline unusable become listing-quality.
The Background Removal Boost
Sometimes what looks blurry is actually just a messy background making the product look fuzzy. Remove the background cleanly at edit-photo.com and the product suddenly reads as sharper.
Not real sharpness—but the visual perception matches.
The Compression Recovery
If your only source is a compressed JPEG (from a supplier, an old backup, a phone that overcompressed), AI can partially reconstruct lost detail.
Not lossless. But often good enough for listing use.
The Prevention Playbook
Going forward, prevent blur:

items.text: Use a tripod for anything longer than 1/60 second
Increase ISO in lower light (accept noise vs blur)
Use continuous shooting mode (3-5 shots, pick the sharpest)
Enable image stabilization on your phone

blocks.text: The Batch Rescue
If you have 50 blurry photos, don't rescue them one by one. Batch:

items.text: Use a separate upscaling or sharpening editor conservatively, then inspect the result at 100% for invented texture and halos.

blocks.text: Some will look great. Some won't. Reshoot only the ones AI can't save.
The Honest Verdict
Sometimes reshooting is the only real solution. But before committing to a full reshoot, test AI rescue on a sample of blurry photos. You might save 60-70% of them and only need to reshoot the rest.
Start Salvaging
Don't reshoot until you've tested rescue options. Try free at edit-photo.com.
